argumentsAgainst: High costs, device dependence and unequal connectivity can deepen the digital divide.
Extended or poorly regulated use may raise concerns involving privacy, safety, accessibility and human well-being.
Immersive presentation does not automatically ensure learning, productivity or inclusion; outcomes depend on design and institutional capacity.
argumentsFor: Immersive interfaces can make complex concepts experiential and support training, simulation, education and public engagement.
They can connect users with digital content in more interactive ways than conventional interfaces.
With inclusive design and safeguards, the technology may support innovation and citizen-facing services.
background: The source title identifies immersive technologies as the subject, but the supplied official summary contains only the words “Immersive Technologies.”
The available extract does not establish a specific programme, institution-led action, application, date of commencement, technology type, funding detail or outcome.
Accordingly, examples such as virtual reality, augmented reality or mixed reality are conceptual illustrations rather than source-established facts.
indiaImplications: India may examine immersive tools for education, skilling, healthcare, industrial training, heritage interpretation and citizen services, subject to evidence of effectiveness.
Public deployment would require affordable access, local-language and disability-inclusive design, data protection, cybersecurity and safeguards against exclusion.
Policymakers should distinguish experimentation from demonstrated public value and require transparent evaluation before scaling.

wayForward: Begin with bounded pilots tied to clearly defined public outcomes rather than novelty.
Publish evaluation metrics covering effectiveness, affordability, accessibility, privacy and safety.
Adopt interoperable and inclusive design standards, including local-language and disability-access requirements.
Strengthen data governance, cybersecurity and user-consent safeguards.
